topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, outlining the scope of the course, student expectations, and lecture learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic, cellular, and structural foundations of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concept of cancer as a progressive breakdown of genetic regulation, cellular differentiation, and tissue architecture.

topics.label: Mechanisms and histological progression of tumor invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how tumors breach tissue boundaries, disseminate through anatomical routes, and progress histologically from benign lesions to invasive malignancies.

topics.label: Tumor classification, nomenclature, and pathophysiological consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how neoplasms are named and categorized, alongside the physiological mechanisms through which benign and malignant tumors cause patient morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Cancer epidemiology and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the incidence and distribution of tumors across human tissues, demographics, and diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Clinical symptoms and screening modalities for early cancer detection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical rationale, histological markers, and practical efficacy of screening methods used to detect pre-malignant and early-stage cancers.

topics.label: Lecture closing and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing, reiterating the learning outcomes and directing students toward upcoming practicals and lectures.
